title: Fuse pulse survival and semiconductor clearing budget
description: Integrate a trapezoidal inrush pulse and compare its thermal integral with fuse pre-arcing allowance, while separately checking total clearing against semiconductor withstand.
formula: Jpulse = Ipk²[thold+(trise+tfall)/3]; Jallow = f Jpre; Jclear = Jpre+Jarc
assumptions: Current starts and ends at zero; rise and fall are linear and the plateau is constant. Total pulse duration is below 10 ms for the short-pulse adiabatic approximation.
Pre-arcing and arcing integrals are manufacturer values for the applicable fault current, voltage, temperature and AC power factor or DC L/R; they are not calculated from the inrush waveform.
The pulse allowance fraction is supplied from the selected fuse's pulse-life and temperature guidance; 0.8 is an illustrative input, not a universal recommendation.
Semiconductor withstand must explicitly be an I²t rating for the applicable pulse conditions. This is not a generic MOSFET or IGBT SOA test.

Negative margins identify failed screening criteria. Voltage rating, interrupting capacity, steady current, arc voltage, repetition and complete time-current coordination require separate checks; this calculation does not certify safety.

constraints.message: The inrush pulse must have positive duration
This adiabatic short-pulse screening model requires a pulse shorter than 10 ms

title: TVS avalanche surge load line
description: Solve the intersection of a resistive surge source and the finite-slope avalanche characteristic of a TVS.
formula: I = (Vs-Vb)/(Rs+rd); Vclamp = Vb+rd I; Ppk = Vclamp I
assumptions: Positive avalanche polarity, a resistive Thevenin surge source, negligible protected-load current, and negligible interconnect inductance.
Breakdown intercept and dynamic resistance are an affine fit at the applicable waveform and temperature, not a universal DC-to-surge conversion.
Calculated current must remain inside the supplied characterized fit-current interval. The pulse-current rating is separately supplied for that exact waveform, duration and temperature.
Peak power is instantaneous, not absorbed energy or a repetitive thermal rating. Negative voltage/current margins are useful failed-design results.
Normal-operation standoff/leakage, negative surges, parasitic overshoot, capacitance, tolerance corners and hardware validation remain separate. No safety or EMC certification is implied.

references.title: Texas Instruments SLVAE37, sections 2.3 and 2.4, Figure 3

constraints.message: The characterized current interval must have positive width
Surge current is below the characterized avalanche-fit interval
Surge current exceeds the characterized avalanche-fit interval

title: MOV nonlinear pulse clamp and absorption
description: Fit a metal-oxide varistor power law between two characterized points and predict clamp voltage, differential resistance and rectangular-pulse absorption within that interval.
formula: beta = ln(V2/V1)/ln(I2/I1); V = V1(I/I1)^beta; rd = beta V/I; E = V I t
assumptions: The two V-I points and pulse belong to the same polarity magnitude, temperature and waveform family in the MOV protection region; 0<beta<1.
Only interpolation between the characterized current endpoints is supported. Do not extrapolate into leakage or high-current bulk-resistance regions.
An imposed constant-current rectangular pulse is used; ideal zero-duration edges contribute no energy. Real edge energy must be included separately or the waveform integrated separately.
The energy allowance is supplied for the same duration, temperature, repetition count and aging condition. Equal joules from different waveforms do not imply equal survival.
The fit neglects self-heating during the pulse, parasitic inductance/capacitance and long-term degradation; it is not a safety certification or thermal-disconnector design.

references.title: Vishay, Varistors: Ideal Solution to Surge Protection, Varistor Operation and Selection Criteria

constraints.message: Upper characterized current must exceed lower current
MOV voltage must rise between characterized points
The MOV protection-region fit requires a sublinear voltage exponent
Pulse current is below the characterized fit interval
Pulse current exceeds the characterized fit interval

title: Zener-triggered SCR crowbar latch window
description: Account for gate-shunt and source loading when finding a crowbar trigger threshold, then check available anode latching current and the holding-current release boundary.
formula: Vtrip = Vz+Vg+(Rs+Rg)(Igt+Vg/Rgk); Ig = (Vfault-Vz-Vg)/(Rs+Rg)-Vg/Rgk; Ia = (Vfault-Von)/Rs; Vrelease = Von+Rs Ih
assumptions: A positive Thevenin fault source feeds the SCR anode through Rs. Anode to gate has series Rg and reverse-biased zener; Rgk shunts gate to cathode. Cathode is the return.
Protected-load current, zener slope resistance and leakage are neglected. Zener and gate drops are constant values at the relevant currents and temperature.
The gate pulse lasts until the SCR anode current reaches the specified latching current. Loop inductance, turn-on time, dI/dt and dV/dt immunity require separate dynamic checks.
After turn-on, Von<Vz turns off the trigger branch. Available anode current is a hypothetical on-state current; a negative latch margin indicates that reliable latching is not established.

The release voltage is a quasi-static holding-current boundary for the assumed constant on-state drop, not a guaranteed turn-off delay. Fuse clearing, SCR surge/SOA, gate power and fault interruption remain separate; no safety certification.

references.title: STMicroelectronics AN4607 Rev 1, sections 1.1, 1.2 and 2.12; manufacturer PDF mirrored by Octopart

title: Copper conductor temperature-limited fault withstand
description: Use the temperature-dependent copper adiabatic heating integral to determine fault-current withstand and the minimum conductor area for a clearing interval.
formula: k = 226 sqrt(ln[(234+Tf)/(234+Ti)]); Iallow = k S/sqrt(t); Jallow=(k S)²; Smin=Ifault sqrt(t)/k
assumptions: S is copper cross-sectional area in mm²; temperatures are degrees Celsius. Material constants 226 A sqrt(s)/mm² and 234 degC come from the cited copper cable adiabatic formula.

This warm-copper cable application is limited to initial temperatures at least 0 degC and final limits at most 250 degC; it does not model cryogenic properties, melting or insulation above that limit.

Uniform conductor current and temperature, negligible heat escape, and a fault-clearing interval of at most 5 s. Skin/proximity effects, joints, contact hotspots and electrodynamic forces are excluded.
Fault current is the equivalent RMS current over the interval; for a nonconstant waveform use its actual integral to establish the equivalent RMS value.

The selected final temperature must also respect the actual insulation and termination ratings; 250 degC is not permission to use that limit for PVC. Negative area margin indicates an undersized conductor. No standards-compliance or safety-certification claim.

references.title: Liban Cables, Generalities section 5.3, copper conductor short-circuit current rating
Schneider Electric Electrical Installation Guide, cable thermal constraints

constraints.message: The permitted final temperature must exceed the initial copper temperature

title: Foldback limiter fault equilibrium and peak pass stress
description: Find a resistive-fault operating point on an affine foldback characteristic and the worst pass-element dissipation anywhere between a short circuit and the current-limit knee.
formula: b=(Ik-Isc)/Vk; I(V)=Isc+bV; Vfault=R Isc/(1-bR); Vstress=clamp[(Vin-Isc/b)/2,0,Vk]; P(V)=(Vin-V)(Isc+bV)
assumptions: The limiter is represented by its characterized affine foldback branch from (V=0,I=Isc) to (V=Vk,I=Ik), not by an uncharacterized transistor or universal regulator formula.
The resistive fault is no larger than Vk/Ik, so its load line has a unique intersection on the foldback branch. The normal voltage-regulation branch is not solved.
A series linear pass element has fixed input voltage greater than the knee voltage. Controller quiescent current and external sense-resistor voltage drop are neglected in pass dissipation.

The quasi-static curve does not predict compensation, oscillations, capacitive startup, transient overshoot or guaranteed recovery with constant-power/current loads; foldback can cause load-dependent latch-up.

The maximum power is taken over the entire characterized foldback voltage interval, not only the short circuit. SOA, current crowding, junction temperature, shutdown timing and fault interruption still require hardware-specific checks; no safety certification.

references.title: onsemi SR005AN/D, Short Circuit Protection, Figures 2 and 3 and foldback latch-up discussion
